doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: The Blue Note album Portrait and a planned Fred Astaire project
summary: She says she was sick during the 1962 Blue Note album, and describes an unrecorded bass-and-voice Fred Astaire tribute with Cameron Brown.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I actually have a piece off that album.
Yeah. And I thought I would just—
I was very sick when I did that album.
Yes. I had an operation when I did that album.

This one? I have a whole new thing on this, with the bass. I do a whole thing on this with all dance tunes, dedicated to Fred Astaire. Bass and voice. Yeah. It’s never been recorded yet. But I will record it one day.
I hope so. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
Yeah. With Cameron. We’ll do it. We just did it last week in Europe, a couple of weeks ago.
